facts.statement: Vegavis geitononesos lived during the Late Cretaceous (Maastrichtian).
facts.quote: Age: Late Cretaceous (Maastrichtian)

facts.statement: The type locality for Vegavis geitononesos is the López de Bertodano Formation.
facts.quote: Type locality: López de Bertodano Formation

facts.statement: Vegavis geitononesos was found in Antarctica.
facts.quote: Country: Antarctica

facts.statement: Vegavis geitononesos was described by Irazoqui et al.
facts.quote: Authors: Irazoqui et al.

facts.statement: Vegavis geitononesos is a newly described species.
facts.quote: Novelty: Sp. nov

facts.statement: Vegavis geitononesos is based on a partial skull and skeleton cataloged as MLP-PV 15-I-7-52.
facts.quote: The authors also named V. geitononesos, a third species in the genus, based on another partial skull and skeleton (MLP-PV 15-I-7-52).

facts.statement: The specific name 'geitononesos' references the discovery of the species on Marambio Island.
facts.quote: The specific name combines the Greek geítōn, meaning neighbor and nêsos, meaning island, referencing the discovery of this species on Marambio Island

facts.statement: The stratum containing Vegavis geitononesos is dated to the uppermost Maastrichtian.
facts.quote: The upper Molluscan Allomember (unit klb 9) of the Lopez de Bertodano Formation on Seymour (Marambio) Island, the type locality of V. geitononesos, is dated to the uppermost Maastrichtian.

facts.statement: Vegavis had a high metabolism that allowed it to survive at high latitudes in Antarctica.
facts.quote: Vegavis was a bird with a high metabolism, which allowed it to live at high latitudes in Antarctica.

facts.statement: Vegavis exhibits osteosclerosis, a condition also found in Polarornis.
facts.quote: It also shows a degree of osteosclerosis, a condition shared with Polarornis.

facts.statement: Vegavis iaai is an extinct bird belonging to the order Anseriformes and the family Vegaviidae, and it is the only known member of the genus Vegavis.
facts.quote: Vegavis iaai es una especie extinta de aves anseriformes de la familia Vegaviidae y único miembro conocido del género Vegavis

facts.statement: The specific name iaai comes from the acronym for the Argentine Antarctic Institute, which leads Argentine scientific expeditions to Antarctica.
facts.quote: El nombre específico iaai, es por las siglas del Instituto Antártico Argentino, que dirige las expediciones científicas argentinas a la Antártica

facts.statement: The type specimen, cataloged as MLP 93-I-3-1, was found in deposits at Cape Lamb on Vega Island, Antarctica, in 1992.
facts.quote: El espécimen, catalogado como MLP 93-I-3-1, fue encontrado en depósitos del Cabo Lamb de la Isla Vega, Antártica, en 1992

facts.statement: The species was only described as new in 2005 because the fossil consists of very delicate remains of a bird embedded in a concretion.
facts.quote: pero solo fue descrito como una nueva especie en 2005 porque consiste de restos muy delicados de un ave embebida en una concreción

facts.statement: The Vegavis fossil specimen is kept in the Museo de La Plata in Argentina.
facts.quote: El espécimen fósil de Vegavis se guarda en el Museo de La Plata, Argentina

facts.statement: Computed axial tomography scans were used to obtain clearer images of the bone structure without risking damage or destruction of the bones.
facts.quote: Se utilizaron escaneos de tomografía axial computarizada (TAC) para ganar en claridad de imagen de la estructura ósea sin correr peligro de dañar o destruir los huesos

facts.statement: Vegavis iaai lived during the Late Cretaceous (Maastrichtian stage) of Antarctica, approximately 65 million years ago.
facts.quote: que vivió durante el Cretácico Superior (estadio Maastrichtiense) de la Antártida, hace unos 65 millones de años

facts.statement: Vegavis belongs to the clade Anseriformes.
facts.quote: Pertenece al clado Anseriformes

facts.statement: Among modern birds, Vegavis is most closely related to the family Anatidae (ducks and geese), but it is not considered a direct ancestor of this family.
facts.quote: Entre las aves modernas, Vegavis está más relacionado con la familia Anatidae (patos y gansos) pero no se considera que sea un ancestro directo de esta

facts.statement: The genus Vegavis lived from 72.2 to 66 million years ago during the Maastrichtian stage.
facts.quote: Time range: Maastrichtian to Maastrichtian (72.2 to 66 million years ago)

facts.statement: The palatine morphology of Vegavis exhibits a combination of primitive and unique characters within Neognathae.
